findings.title: Bulk sensitive data exposure
findings.description: An endpoint returns a list of records with personal or financial fields, and it is either reachable without a token or not documented, so nobody reviewed what it hands out.
findings.detail: GET /owners (customers-service) returns a list with pii fields
findings.owasp: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization
findings.recommendation: Reduce fields and require an admin role on /owners.
mitigation: Return only the fields the client needs (response schema / DTO, not the raw record).
Paginate with a hard maximum and require an admin role for bulk export.
Log every bulk export with the caller identity.

findings.title: Sensitive operation answers anonymous callers
findings.description: Requests with no credential at all got a 2xx response from an endpoint that returns sensitive data or changes state.
findings.detail: GET /owners (customers-service) returned 2xx to 45 request(s) without a token
factors: likelihood +1: anonymous success seen on the public path
findings.recommendation: Add authentication to GET /owners in customers-service.
mitigation: Require a verified token on this operation in the service itself, not only at the gateway.
Reject requests without Authorization with 401 before any business logic runs.
Add a test that calls the endpoint anonymously and expects 401.

findings.title: Gateway route forwards requests without authentication
findings.description: A gateway route is configured with no authentication and forwards to endpoints that are not login endpoints, so the gateway is not acting as an authentication boundary.
findings.detail: route /api/customer/** -> customers-service has auth: none
evidence: exposes: GET /api/customer/owners, POST /api/customer/owners, GET /api/customer/owners/{ownerId}, PUT /api/customer/owners/{ownerId}, POST /api/customer/owners/{ownerId}/pets, GET /api/customer/owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}, PUT /api/customer/owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}, GET /api/customer/petTypes
findings.recommendation: Set auth: required on gateway route /api/customer.
mitigation: Set auth: required on the route, or split public paths (login) into their own route.
Deny by default: routes without an explicit auth setting should be rejected at deploy time.
findings.snippet:
routes:
  - prefix: /api/payments
    service: payment-service
    auth: required      # was: none

findings.title: Public entry serves the API without TLS
findings.description: The public entry (Ingress, load balancer, Istio Gateway or published port) has no TLS, so Authorization headers and personal data sent through it can be read or replayed on the network. The evidence says how many public endpoints carried them in this capture.
findings.detail: published port (docker compose) api-gateway serves the API over plain HTTP
findings.recommendation: Enable TLS on published port (docker compose) api-gateway.
mitigation: Terminate TLS at the ingress (tls: section + certificate) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Send Strict-Transport-Security so browsers never fall back to HTTP.
findings.snippet:
spec:
  tls:
    - hosts: [api.example.com]
      secretName: api-tls

findings.title: Service-to-service call accepted without credentials
findings.description: Another microservice calls this endpoint without any credential and it succeeds, so any pod that can reach it can do the same (no zero-trust between services).
findings.detail: genai-service -> GET /owners (customers-service) with no credential
evidence: no mTLS enforced for customers-service (no STRICT PeerAuthentication or mesh injection)
findings.recommendation: Require service identity (mTLS or a service token) on /owners in customers-service.
mitigation: Authenticate workloads to each other: mTLS through a service mesh, or signed service tokens.
Authorize per caller: only order-service may call /charge, for example.
findings.snippet:
# Istio: require mTLS and allow only order-service
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
spec:
  rules:
  - from:
    - source: {principals: ["cluster.local/ns/shoplite/sa/order-service"]}

findings.title: Calls from an unidentified internal caller
findings.description: Traces start at this backend endpoint, so the caller is not instrumented and did not come through the gateway. Monitoring cannot say who made these calls.
findings.detail: 5 trace(s) start at admin-server GET /applications with no traced caller
evidence: no parent span from the gateway or another service
findings.recommendation: Identify and instrument the caller of GET /applications.
mitigation: Instrument every job and client that calls internal APIs (propagate traceparent).
Require caller identity on internal endpoints so logs name the caller.

findings.title: Calls to a third-party API seen in traces
findings.description: A service calls a host outside the system. Data from it should be validated like user input.
findings.detail: genai-service calls external openai-api
findings.recommendation: Validate responses from openai-api in genai-service.
mitigation: Validate and size-limit third-party responses; use TLS and timeouts.
Keep an inventory of third-party APIs and their data.

findings.title: No network segmentation for the service
findings.description: No NetworkPolicy selects this workload, so every pod in the cluster can call it. One compromised pod can move laterally.
findings.detail: admin-server accepts traffic from any pod
evidence: callers seen in traces: none (only external clients)
findings.recommendation: Add a NetworkPolicy for admin-server allowing only: the ingress controller.
mitigation: Add a default-deny NetworkPolicy for the namespace, then allow only the callers seen in traces.

steps.title: Set auth: required on gateway route /api/customer.
mitigation: Set auth: required on the route, or split public paths (login) into their own route.
Deny by default: routes without an explicit auth setting should be rejected at deploy time.

steps.title: Enforce authentication and role checks on GET /owners (customers-service)
mitigation: Return only the fields the client needs (response schema / DTO, not the raw record).
Paginate with a hard maximum and require an admin role for bulk export.
Log every bulk export with the caller identity.
Require a verified token on this operation in the service itself, not only at the gateway.
Reject requests without Authorization with 401 before any business logic runs.
Add a test that calls the endpoint anonymously and expects 401.
Authenticate workloads to each other: mTLS through a service mesh, or signed service tokens.
Authorize per caller: only order-service may call /charge, for example.
